Specification of Communication Management
AUTOSAR AP R25-11
[SWS_CM_00140] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for transmission requests
for Triggers
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each trigger shall have
a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see
ServiceInterfaceDeploymentEle-
ment
.
minimumSendInterval
), which specifies the minimum amount of time that
shall pass between two consecutive transmissions, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval
limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given trigger in the network. If the application
requests transmission of a trigger by calling
Trigger::Send()/Send()
,
ara::com
shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the trigger to the
underlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e.,
the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the trigger has never been sent before, this
shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send
Interval is not violated,
ara::com
shall process the transmission request by handing
over the trigger to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start
of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is vio-
lated,
ara::com
shall discard the transmission request and return error
ComErrc::
kMinimumSendIntervalViolationError
(see [SWS_CM_10432]). If the config-
ured Minimum Send Interval (
ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement
.
minimum-
SendInterval
) of a trigger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring
shall not be active for the corresponding trigger.
⌋
